newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Western consortium wins Kazakh copper plant tender.
newsitem.headline: Western consortium wins Kazakh copper plant tender.

text.p: A consortium grouping Glencore AG of Switzerland, Phelps Dodge Corp of the U.S. and Kazkommerzbank won a tender for 85 percent of Kazakhstan's copper plant AO Balkhashmys, a state official said on Thursday.

Baurzhan Begimbetov, spokesman for the State Property Committee, said the consortium had agreed to invest $650 million in the facility by 2005, raise copper output to 180,000 tonnes a year in 1997 and pay off the plant's $90 million debt.
He did not say how much the consortium paid for the stake, but said it beat Britain's Trans World Group in the tender.

Switzerland's Cam Finance S.A. won a tender to buy 29 percent of Balkhashmys in December 1995 and pledged to invest $510 million over seven to eight years, but Begimbetov said the government cancelled the deal when terms were not met.

Balkhashmys, formally known as Balkhashmet, was put under the management of Kazcommerzbank, one of Kazakhstan's largest private banks, in August because of its large debts and officials said then that the plant would either be declared bankrupt or retendered.
Cam Finance could not be reached for immediate comment.
The facility, which accounted for about 40 percent of Kazakh copper output in earlier years, produced about 125,000 tonnes of copper cathode in 1995.
But its August 1996 output slipped to 6,800 tonnes.
The former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan sits on the world's third largest copper reserves.
